threads.body: This guard treats any `langgraph_node` metadata as proof that the resolved name is an internal node. A legitimate chain/runnable named `SupportAgentRunner` nested in a graph with `metadata={"langgraph_node": "model"}` is therefore not classified as `invoke_agent` and can fall through to workflow/None, contrary to the new name-based behavior. Limit the exception to when the resolved name is the node being classified (and add a regression test).

@@ -159,6 +159,19 @@ def _has_agent_signals(
     )
 
 
+def _detect_agent_name(
+    agent_name: str | None,
+    metadata: dict[str, Any] | None,
+) -> bool:
+    """Return whether a chain name identifies an agent-like runnable."""
+    if not agent_name or "agent" not in agent_name.lower():
+        return False
+
+    # A LangGraph node named "agent" is internal graph plumbing, not proof
+    # that the graph itself represents an agent.
+    return not (metadata and metadata.get(LANGGRAPH_NODE_KEY))

threads.body: This adds a user-visible span-mapping rule: root `AgentExecutor` and named runnables can now emit `invoke_agent`, but the package README still describes agent spans only as invocations nested inside a workflow and does not document name-based detection. Please update the README to explain the heuristic and root-agent behavior so users can predict the new spans.
